newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Westpac says BankMelb integral to plans.
newsitem.headline: Westpac says BankMelb integral to plans.

text.p: Westpac Banking Corp would complete its strategy of strengthening its presence in several key markets if its planned takeover of Bank of Melbourne Ltd was successful, Westpac managing director Bob Joss said on Monday.
Joss told a Securities Institute luncheon in Sydney that Westpac had in 1993 identified New Zealand, Victoria and Western Australia as the key regional markets where Westpac was not strong enough.
He said the A$1.435 billion Bank of Melbourne purchase would complete that process of strengthening its presence in those markets.
This followed its NZ$1.3 billion takeover of New Zealand's Trust Bank network in 1996 and its late-1995 A$689 million purchase of Western Australia's Challenge Bank.
"That (the Bank of Melbourne purchase) really does then address the overall market and our needs in terms of strategy," Joss said.
Anti-monopolies watchdog, the Australian Competition and Consumer Competition (ACCC), has said it will rule on the Bank of Melbourne-Westpac takeover by the end of April or early May.
The ACCC told Westpac informally in late 1995 it could not take over Bank of Melbourne and has ruled since that there should be at least one regional bank in each state.
Bank of Melbourne is the last significant regional bank in Victoria.
